tagline: First US lunar orbiter (1966-08-14); mapped Apollo landing sites and took the first photo of Earth from lunar orbit (1966).
description: The first US spacecraft to orbit the Moon, four months after Luna 10. Launched 1966-08-10 from Cape Canaveral on an Atlas-Agena D, Lunar Orbiter 1 entered an elliptical lunar orbit on 1966-08-14. Its primary mission was to photograph candidate Apollo landing sites at sub-metre resolution — a 70 mm + 610 mm dual-lens camera system that developed film in-orbit (Bimat process) and scanned it for radio transmission to Earth. Captured the first photograph of Earth from lunar orbit (1966-08-23 — over two years before Apollo 8's more famous Earthrise) as a wide-angle shot taken during the 16th orbit. Returned 207 high-resolution + 207 medium-resolution frames mapping 4.1 million km² of the lunar surface. Deliberately crashed into the lunar far side on 1966-10-29 to clear the radio band for Lunar Orbiter 2.
best_known_for: First US lunar orbiter (1966-08-14). Mapped potential Apollo landing sites; took the first photograph of Earth from lunar orbit — over two years before the famous Apollo 8 Earthrise
